findings.finding: Vary wall thickness while holding a hollow cylinder's outer radius and length fixed.
findings.breakdown: The sequence distinguishes wall thickness from inner radius and tests whether equal increases in thickness produce equal increases in material volume.
findings.checked: Using V = π[R² − (R − t)²]L, the three volumes are 90π, 160π and 210π cm³. Successive increases are 70π and 50π cm³. The follow-up has inner radius 3 cm and outer radius 5 cm, giving 128π cm³. All radii are positive. Cylinder volume is rehearsed in p3-q1-e, subtraction is taught in p4-definition-block, and hollow cylinders appear in p6-q3-a and p6-q3-f.
findings.assumptions: Students use the taught subtraction method; no algebraic generalisation is required.

repair.proposal: Immediately after p6-q3-f: 'Before calculating, predict whether each extra centimetre of wall thickness adds the same material volume. Find the material volume of pipes with outer radius 5 cm and length 10 cm, whose wall thicknesses are (a) 1 cm, (b) 2 cm, (c) 3 cm. Compare successive increases and explain your prediction.' Expected volumes: 90π, 160π and 210π cm³; increases: 70π and 50π cm³. Outer radius and length stay fixed; thickness varies. Follow with: 'A pipe has inner diameter 6 cm, wall thickness 2 cm and length 8 cm. Find its material volume.' Expected answer: 128π cm³.

findings.doneWhen: The optional sequence includes prediction, three thickness variations, comparison of volume increases and the unpatterned follow-up.

findings.finding: Explain why two different decompositions of the same stepped prism give the same volume.
findings.breakdown: The task returns to the introductory stepped prism and asks students to justify why different valid splits preserve its volume.
findings.checked: Both expressions simplify to L[aH + Wh − ah]. With 0 < a < W, 0 < h < H and L > 0, both decompositions contain positive component dimensions and cover the solid exactly once. The geometric explanation uses the decomposition and addition method taught in p4-definition-block and p4-example-block.
findings.assumptions: Symbolic expansion is prior algebra knowledge supported by the course's separate algebra booklets; students can also justify equality geometrically.

repair.proposal: Optional early-finisher task after p9-q13: 'A stepped prism has total cross-section width W, left width a, left height H, right height h and length L, where 0 < a < W, 0 < h < H and L > 0. Split it into two side-by-side rectangular prisms, then into a full-width lower prism and an upper-left prism. Write both volume expressions and explain why they agree.' Expected answer: L[aH + (W − a)h] and L[Wh + a(H − h)] both simplify to L[aH + Wh − ah]. Both splits cover the same solid without gaps or overlap.

findings.doneWhen: The optional task specifies valid dimensions and includes both volume expressions and an explanation of their equality.
